newsitem.title: ECUADOR: SOCCER-ASPRILLA STRIKES AGAIN AS COLOMBIA BEAT ECUADOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ASPRILLA STRIKES AGAIN AS COLOMBIA BEAT ECUADOR.

text.p: Faustino Asprilla scored his sixth goal in five World Cup qualifiers to give Colombia a 1-0 win over Ecuador on Wednesday.
The victory kept them top of the South American qualifying competition.
Asprilla struck in the 72nd minute with a spectacular effort to end a 100 percent home record for Ecuador, coached by former Colombia national team boss Francisco Maturana.
The Newcastle striker blasted an angled shot into the net after being set up by substitute Anthony de Avila to silence a sellout 45,000 crowd at the Atahualpa stadium.
Ecuador, who have never played in the World Cup finals, began the day second in the single South American group thanks to three home wins. Their victims included Argentina.

Colombia had more possession in the first half but Ecuador looked more dangerous, with goalkeeper Farid Mondragon forced to make several difficult saves from strikers Eduardo Hurtado and Brazilian-born Gilson de Souza.

Colombia became more incisive after coach Hernan Dario Gomez, Maturana's assistant in the last two World Cups, brought on de Avila and Harold Lozano for Brazilian-based Freddy Rincon and Victor Hugo Aristizabal in the 61st minute.
The rarified air of Quito, which lies 2,800 metres above sea level, seemed to have little effect on Colombia who pressed for a second goal towards the end as the home team ran out of attacking ideas.
Colombia itself came to a near standstill during the game, played in the middle of the day local time, with public and private companies shutting up shot for two hours.
Thousands watched the match on giant screens erected in public squares around the country. Even president Ernesto Samper interrupted an engagement to watch the game with his advisers.
The result gave Colombia, with four wins and a draw in five games, a four-point lead over Ecuador, who stayed second in the group despite the defeat.
The top four in the nine-team group qualify for the 1998 World Cup finals.

Ecuador - Carlos Morales, Wagner Rivera, Alberto Montano, Maximo Tenorio, Luis Capurro, Hector Carabali, Ivan Hurtado (Alfonso Obregon, 62nd), Agustin Delgado, Alex Aguinaga, Gilson de Souza (Angel Fernandez, 70th), Eduardo Hurtado.

Colombia - Farid Mondragon, Hugo Galeano, Jorge Bermudez, Osman Lopez, Wilmer Cabrera, Leonel Alvarez, Mauricio Serna, Carlos Valderrama, Freddy Rincon (Anthony de Avila, 61st), Victor Hugo Aristizabal (Harold Lozano 61st), Faustino Asprilla.
